To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a first order transition in compact stars is disfavored by the data, but that the data cannot rule out a crossover transition.

(1) the mass-radius data for 2 M⊙ compact stars are compatible with both a crossover and a first-order transition in the core of neutron stars, (2) a first-order transition is preferred by the Bayesian analysis, (3) the mass-radius constraints are not yet precise enough to determine whether a crossover or a first-order transition occurs, (4) the mass of the maximum mass star is not a good discriminator between a crossover and a phase transition in the core, and (5

(i) the probability distribution of the pressure at saturation density for the nuclear matter equation of state is very narrow, (ii) the probability of a first order deconfinement phase transition is very low, (iii) the probability of the existence of a critical end point is low, and (iv) the pressure at saturation is compatible with the empirical value from nuclear physics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two main topics:   1.
the question of the existence of the critical point in the QCD matter phase diagram and how to constrain its location in a model-independent way.
the question whether the existence of a critical point in QCD is reflected in the properties of compact stars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data do not allow to rule out a first order transition in the interior of neutron stars, but they are consistent with crossover as well.
the present data do not rule out a crossover transition.
the Bayesian analysis of the mass-radius constraints does not provide evidence for a first order deconfinement phase transition in the core of compact stars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Bayesian approach is able to provide probability distributions for the equation of state parameters and that these distributions are sensitive to the choice of the underlying phase transition scenario.
we can constrain the EoS for compact stars with a high accuracy, and the results do not change significantly when we include a first order transition into the analysis.
a deconfinemement transition is not required to explain the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bayesian analysis of mass and radius data alone cannot distinguish between crossover and first order transitions.
the Bayesian approach is a powerful tool to extract probability distributions for equations of state.
a crossover transition in the EoS of compact stars does not seem to be supported by present data.
